title: QCOM data by YCharts On February 5, Broadcom ( AVGO ) confi
text:
QCOM data by YCharts 
On February 5, Broadcom ( AVGO ) confirmed its "best and final offer" for Qualcomm ( QCOM ) at $82/share. The offer is a cash and shares offer, which includes $60 in cash and $22 in AVGO shares. The offer is also premised on Qualcomm either completing the NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ) transaction at $110 or walking away.
As a Qualcomm shareholder, I am willing to take that offer. I have no affinity for AVGO - I would sell those shares as soon as I received them or sell my Qualcomm shares if they hit $82 on the deal.
Qualcomm's management hasn't shown an ability to work within the law - antitrust fines continue to pile up. Management has also not shown any ability to mend ties with customers - relationships with Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) and another licensee remain contentious.
In my DCF below, I value Qualcomm at $80/share, excluding the impact of the FTC and the Apple litigation. Including those, I would adjust that range to $80-$90. But given the uncertainty of those outcomes, and my lack of faith in management until they show positive signs of improving customer relations, I will reluctantly take the $82.
Licensing Disputes and Fines Qualcomm's results over the past year or more have been dominated by news of licensing disputes and fines. In FY2017, Qualcomm was fined $854 million in Korea for antitrust violations, $774 million in Taiwan for antitrust violations, and lost $815 million to BlackBerry ( BB ) in a licensing royalty dispute.
